record.tranche_reason: The study trains a CNN on random-label classification and reports training accuracy reaching 100%, directly bearing on whether such networks fit random labels.
record.gate_note: The study's transfer-time results concern pretraining and fine-tuning efficiency; they do not compare random-label and true-label training time or vary the fraction of corrupted labels. The fixed random-pixel experiment is relevant to unstructured inputs. Cited results from prior work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly measures random-label training accuracy for a standard CNN trained with SGD and reports near-perfect fitting. Its transfer experiments do not compare learning true versus random labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. More precisely, equivalent transfer occurs with shared image distributions; mismatched random-pixel pretraining can yield non-equivalent transfer. Ablations attribute fully connected transfer to weight magnitude and convolutional transfer partly to covariance structure. Conclusions are limited to one seven-layer CNN and CIFAR-10.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a standard CNN with SGD on random labels, but focuses on transfer between memorization tasks rather than reproducing the original study's broader tests of generalization, test error, and regularization.
record.method_sensitivity: Transfer depends on upstream task consistency and distribution: resampling labels prevents transfer, while resampling random-pixel data weakens but preserves it. Transfer also differs between shared-image, shared-distribution, and random-pixel settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Fixed uniform random-pixel pretraining accelerates downstream random-label fitting, but its final upstream fitting accuracy is unreported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretraining on a mismatched random-input task can accelerate downstream memorization.

fits_no_version.finding: With random pixels resampled every epoch, upstream accuracy stays at chance while downstream transfer persists in weakened form.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transfer can arise without memorizing a fixed upstream dataset.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2026 workshop: Neural Network Artifacts as a New Data Modality
record.problems: Only one architecture and base dataset are tested. Several supporting experiments are shown as figures, and representative seeds are used for some weight-rescaling demonstrations. The paper focuses on training dynamics and does not report test error or true-label generalization.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant numerical rows beyond the random-label fit and random-pixel input results were extracted. Transfer-time curves in Figures 2–10 do not test the listed versions' training-time comparison, label-noise sweep, regularization effects, or learning order.

untested.parts: Chance test error and fitting without changing architecture or hyperparameters relative to true-label training are not measured.
No comparison of true-label and random-label fitting times, or convergence-time sweep over corruption fractions.
Zero training error on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian inputs is not demonstrated. Final fitting accuracy for fixed uniform random pixels is also not reported.
No corruption-fraction sweep measuring training fit and test-error degradation.
No regularization comparisons or true-label generalization measurements. Successful fitting without weight decay or augmentation does not test whether these prevent fitting when present.
No comparison of the learning order of real patterns and noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: Neither an unreported upstream endpoint nor chance accuracy on continually replaced inputs warrants a limits_scope verdict for V3. Transfer-time and weight-ablation results do not test V2 or V6.

versions.untested_parts: Test error at chance and comparison with generalization on true labels are not reported.
The study does not compare training time for random and true labels or sweep the fraction of corrupted labels.
The study tests random-pixel inputs, but not shuffled pixels or independently permuted pixels.
No sweep from no label noise to all labels corrupted with test error measurements.
No comparison of weight decay, dropout, or augmentation effects on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
No measurement of whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.
